diagnosis.summary: The nightly ingest for 2026-10-01 failed because the order_items landing file (landing/order_items/dt=2026-10-01/order_items.csv) was never delivered. The other tables landed normally and the path and naming are unchanged, so this looks like a one-off upstream export gap. I proposed redelivery of orders, order_items and payments for 2026-10-01, followed by a rerun.

root_cause.explanation: The order_items CSV for dt=2026-10-01 is absent, although the partition directory exists. customers, orders and payments landed with clean headers and normal volumes. order_items landed fine on 09-30 under the same path and naming. The ingest config is at defaults and no model changed. This points to a one-off delivery gap, not a schema or path change.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed because the order_items landing file is missing
Only order_items is missing for 10-01. Other tables are normal, and order_items was fine on 09-30 with the same path.
The runbook prescribes redelivery of orders, order_items and payments together for a missing file

alternatives_considered: Path or naming change by upstream: unlikely, since the path is unchanged and the other tables are fine. The worker could not list the contents of the 10-01 directory, so this is not fully ruled out.
Ingest config mapping problem: config is at defaults and the error is a missing file, not a column issue.
Bad dbt model deploy: the failure is at ingest, before any transform ran.
rerun_only: would fail again because the file is still absent.
Escalate to upstream_app_team: reserve for the case where redelivery returns the same missing file.

proposal.rationale: order_items landing file for 2026-10-01 is missing while the other tables and prior days are fine and path/naming is unchanged: a one-off delivery gap. Runbook says to redeliver all related tables together, then rerun.

applied: upstream re-exported orders (440 rows), order_items (840 rows), payments (417 rows) for 2026-10-01
